title: Solo 401(k) vs. SEP-IRA Optimizer
description: Self-employed retirement-contribution comparator: the maximum Solo 401(k), SEP-IRA and SIMPLE IRA contribution under one dated set of IRS limits, each plan's binding cap, a winner ranked by maximum contribution with a declared tie order, and the estimated tax saving at a caller-supplied marginal rate. The tax year is an explicit as_of input, never a clock. Money is integer cents with floor division. No Date, no floats, no network.

tax_year.description: Four-digit tax year selecting the pinned IRS limit table (2026 only). An input, never a clock; other years are refused.

net_income_usd_cents.description: Net self-employment profit in integer cents, 1..20000000000. Zero is refused (Apex silently defaulted 0 to 120000; DIFFERS D2).

age.description: Age at end of tax year, 18..120. Decides the 414(v) and SECURE 2.0 catch-up bands; band edges pinned by boundary fixtures.

marginal_rate_bp.description: Marginal rate in basis points of one, 0..10000 (2400 = 24%). Zero is honoured; Apex coerced 0 to 24% (DIFFERS D5).

existing_employer_plan.description: Boolean. Echoed and flagged, never used in the arithmetic (Apex read it and ignored it; DIFFERS D4).

existing_deferrals_cents.description: Elective deferrals already made to an outside employer plan this year, 0..72000000; reduces 402(g) deferral room.

output_schema.description: output_payload: tax_year, net_income_usd_cents, self_employment_tax_base_usd_cents, self_employment_tax_usd_cents, half_se_tax_deduction_usd_cents, net_earnings_after_half_deduction_usd_cents, age, marginal_rate_bp, catchup_eligible, super_catchup_band, existing_employer_plan, existing_deferrals_cents, solo_401k{employee_deferral_usd_cents, catchup_usd_cents, employer_contribution_usd_cents, max_total_usd_cents, tax_savings_usd_cents, binding_caps{employee_deferral, employer_contribution, total}}, sep_ira{max_total_usd_cents, tax_savings_usd_cents, binding_caps{contribution}}, simple_ira{employee_usd_cents, employer_nonelective_usd_cents, max_total_usd_cents, tax_savings_usd_cents, binding_caps{employee}}, ranking[{plan, max_total_usd_cents}], winner, winner_tied, winner_tie_order, refusal_reason, domain_errors[], scope_note.

input_schema_provenance: Top-level properties are exactly the policy_parameters members the kernel reads, one per read, every one of them unconditionally dereferenced after validation: tax_year (LIMITS_BY_TAX_YEAR lookup plus SUPPORTED_TAX_YEAR gate), net_income_usd_cents (seBase, seTax, halfDeduction, netEarnings, and the SIMPLE employee clamp), age (both catch-up band tests), marginal_rate_bp (all three tax_savings terms), existing_employer_plan (echoed and flagged, deliberately outside the arithmetic), existing_deferrals_cents (deferralRoom). No property carries a placeholder type; no kernel read is missing a schema entry.
author: PostOakLabs

output_example.scope_note: Estimates maximum CONTRIBUTION ceilings, not after-tax wealth. The marginal rate is a caller input, so tax_savings are a rate-times-contribution identity, not a projection. Not modelled: the Social Security wage base (Pub 505 2026 Worksheet 2-3 caps the 12.4% portion at $184,500, so the true SE rate falls below 15.3% above that base); the employer 25% ceiling measured on compensation net of the employee deferral; SIMPLE $18,100 small-employer limits and the 402(g) aggregation across an outside employer plan; the $400 net-earnings SE-tax floor; Roth catch-up wage thresholds; and plan administration, actuarial or audit cost. Amounts are integer cents with floor division; the Apex source page used IEEE-754 doubles and rounded for display, so sub-cent intermediates differ by construction.
